articles.body: Webform and Webform REST Flaws in the September 2026 Drupal Advisory Two related projects, two advisories Advisory WID-SEC-2026-3554 covers contributed Drupal projects, and two of them belong to the same family. Webform is a widely installed module for building submission forms, and Webform REST exposes those submissions through a REST interface. The advisory lists fixed releases for both. Webform is fixed in 6.2.12 and 6.3.1, covering two maintenance branches. Webform REST is fixed in 4.2.1. Webform installations are common enough that the flaw class deserves attention on its own, because a form module is by design reachable by anonymous visitors. Why a form module carries risk A form builder accepts input from anyone who can reach the form.

articles.title: A million-tap linear-phase FIR in real time: 7 ms of plumbing, 650 ms of filter
articles.excerpt: I'm building Sonir Bench, a macOS app that captures everything your Mac plays, runs it through a DSP chain you design, and sends it to your DAC. The first post in this series was the overview. This on…
articles.body: I'm building Sonir Bench, a macOS app that captures everything your Mac plays, runs it through a DSP chain you design, and sends it to your DAC. The first post in this series was the overview. This one goes deep on a single piece: long FIR convolution. Here's the result up front. On an M6 Mac mini, I ran a 998,545-tap linear-phase FIR at 768 kHz in f64 for almost eight hours. Zero dropouts: no underruns, no overruns, no missed deadlines. The round-trip latency was 657.43 ms. But 650.09 ms of that is the filter's own group delay. The machinery that moves the audio adds only 7.33 ms. It took me a few wrong turns to learn to keep those two numbers apart.

articles.title: Building App Logging Alerts with Custom Polling Tools Explained
articles.excerpt: When you compare app logging tools with alerts against polling, a pricing rollout has one unforgiving constraint: after a disputed order, the team must reconstruct the rule decision that the shopper r…
articles.body: When you compare app logging tools with alerts against polling, a pricing rollout has one unforgiving constraint: after a disputed order, the team must reconstruct the rule decision that the shopper received. An alert saying error count > 10 cannot do that. TL;DR: Emit one structured decision event for each price calculation, preserve a stable correlation ID, and alert on both explicit failures and missing expected events. Compare a managed log-alert service with a polling worker by replaying the same incident questions. Choose the design that returns defensible evidence with the least operational glue, not the longest feature list or smallest advertised number. This changes the usual logging-tools discussion.

articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: Watch SpaceX launch classified mission for the US Space Force today
articles.excerpt: SpaceX will launch a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15), and you can watch the action live.
articles.body: SpaceX will launch a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force this evening (Oct. 15), and you can watch the action live. A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to lift off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today, on California's beautiful but frequently fog-blanketed central coast, during a four-hour window that opens at 7:44 p.m. EDT (2344 GMT; 4:44 p.m. local time). You can watch it live via a SpaceX webcast , which is expected to begin about 10 minutes before launch. This evening's launch will kick off the USSF-481 mission, which will deliver mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier. Don't expect SpaceX to provide more info during the webcast.

articles.body: 6 Min Read NASA Satellites Observe Historic 2026 El Niño This visualization compares three ocean data products, sea surface temperature anomaly, apparent visible wavelength, and sea surface height anomaly, over the same months in 2025 and 2026. Signals of El Niño in each map are highlighted with pop-up labels. Credits: NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio A phenomenon rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system is unfolding this fall, and NASA is tracking it closely. El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges roughly every two to seven years marked by warmer-than-normal water temperatures in parts of the equatorial Pacific.

articles.title: Vaonis unveils Atlas, the world's 1st modular smart telescope system
articles.excerpt: Pre-orders are now open for the Atlas, the new modular smart telescope from Vaonis which allows observation with two optical tubes.
articles.body: Vaonis has just announced its new generation of smart telescope technology, known as Atlas. Less of a single smart telescope and more of a new optical system, Atlas was designed with interchangeability and adaptability in mind. Its new SkyDock system allows two optical tubes to be connected and the telescope has live night sky monitoring to predict available observations. You can preorder the Vaonis Atlas with a single Atlas 80 module for $3,990, or $5,490 for the twin at Adorama . But it'll also soon be available at B&H and other retailers. Currently, there is only one optical tube, the Atlas 80, but Vaonis is planning to release add-on modules designed for looking at different night sky objects, including for planetary observation.
